title: What Each Modifier Means
blurb: Start with the individual keywords, then the two combined ones. Match each access modifier to exactly who can reach the member.

levels.title: L1 · The four individual ones
levels.prompt: Match each single keyword to what it allows.

right.label: any code in the same assembly

failStates.title: protected is about inheritance, not the assembly
failStates.explain: protected opens the member to derived classes (in any assembly), NOT to every class in the same assembly. 'Same assembly' is what internal means.

failStates.title: internal is about the assembly, not inheritance
failStates.explain: internal means 'anyone in this assembly.' A derived class in another assembly can't see it. Inheritance-based access is protected.

levels.title: L2 · The two combined ones
levels.prompt: The compound modifiers are the confusing part. One is OR, one is AND — match them up.

right.label: same assembly OR a derived class anywhere
a derived class, but only in the same assembly
any code in the same assembly

failStates.title: protected internal is the OR (the widest)
failStates.explain: protected internal = protected OR internal — the most permissive: any class in the assembly, plus derived classes anywhere. The AND (narrowest) one is private protected.

failStates.title: private protected is the AND (the narrowest)
failStates.explain: private protected = protected AND internal — you must be BOTH a derived class AND in the same assembly. That's the most restrictive combination.
